en.question: In how many ways can a \( 2 \times 6 \) rectangular board be completely tiled using indistinguishable \( 1 \times 2 \) dominoes?
en.hint: Condition on the rightmost column: either one vertical domino (\( T_{n-1} \)) or two horizontal dominoes (\( T_{n-2} \)).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Use the Fibonacci recurrence T_n = T_{n-1} + T_{n-2} with T_1 = 1 and T_2 = 2.

Step 1: Let \( T_k \) be the number of tilings of a \( 2 \times k \) board. Then \( T_1 = 1 \) and \( T_2 = 2 \).

Step 2: Every tiling of \( 2 \times k \) ends with either \( 1 \) vertical domino or \( 2 \) stacked horizontal dominoes, so \( T_k = T_{k-1} + T_{k-2} \).

Step 3: Iterating up to \( k = 6 \) gives the sequence \( 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 \), so \( T_{6} = 13 \).

✅ Quick Check: Check: \( T_{5} + T_{4} = 8 + 5 = 13 \).

💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نستخدم العلاقة التراجعية لفيبوناتشي T_n = T_{n-1} + T_{n-2} مع القيمتين الابتدائيتين T_1 = 1 وT_2 = 2.

الخطوة 3: بحساب الحدود متتالية نجد \( T_{6} = 13 \).

en.question: A \( 1 \times 5 \) strip is tiled using \( 1 \times 1 \) squares available in \( 1 \) color(s) and \( 1 \times 2 \) dominoes available in \( 2 \) color(s). How many distinct colored tilings are possible?
en.hint: Set up the linear recurrence \( a_k = 1a_{k-1} + 2a_{k-2} \) with \( a_0 = 1 \) and \( a_1 = 1 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Condition on the last tile placed to build the weighted second-order recurrence a_k = p*a_{k-1} + q*a_{k-2}.

Step 1: If the last tile is a \( 1 \times 1 \) square (\( 1 \) choices), there are \( 1a_{k-1} \) completions; if it is a \( 1 \times 2 \) domino (\( 2 \) choices), there are \( 2a_{k-2} \) completions.

Step 2: Starting from \( a_0 = 1 \) and \( a_1 = 1 \), apply \( a_k = 1a_{k-1} + 2a_{k-2} \).

Step 3: The terms for \( k = 1, \dots, 5 \) are \( 1, 3, 5, 11, 21 \), giving \( a_{5} = 21 \).

✅ Quick Check: Final step check: \( 1 \cdot 11 + 2 \cdot 5 = 21 \).

en.question: In an Intermediate Olympiad tiling recurrence problem, how many ways can a \( 3 \times 6 \) grid be completely tiled with \( 1 \times 2 \) dominoes?
en.hint: Let \( A_{2k} \) be full tilings of \( 3 \times 2k \); eliminating corner-missing states yields \( A_{2k} = 4A_{2k-2} - A_{2k-4} \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Use coupled state recurrences A_{2k} = 3 A_{2k-2} + 2 B_{2k-3}, which reduces to A_{2k} = 4 A_{2k-2} - A_{2k-4}.

Step 1: For \( 3 \times 2k \) boards, base cases are \( A_0 = 1 \) and \( A_2 = 3 \).

Step 2: Coupling full columns \( A_{2k} \) and protruding-domino states gives the recurrence \( A_{2k} = 4A_{2k-2} - A_{2k-4} \).

Step 3: Computing sequentially gives \( A_{0} = 1, A_{2} = 3, A_{4} = 11, A_{6} = 41 \), so \( A_{6} = 41 \).

✅ Quick Check: Notice \( A_{6} = 41 > 3^{3} = 27 \) because dominoes can straddle the boundaries between \( 3 \times 2 \) blocks.

ar.question: في مسألة علاقات تراجعية للأولمبياد المتوسط، بكم طريقة يمكن تبليط شبكة أبعادها \( 3 \times 6 \) بالكامل باستخدام قطع دومينو \( 1 \times 2 \)؟
ar.hint: ليكن \( A_{2k} \) عدد تبليطات الشبكة \( 3 \times 2k \)؛ بحذف الحالات المساعدة تنتج العلاقة \( A_{2k} = 4A_{2k-2} - A_{2k-4} \).

💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نستخدم العلاقات التراجعية المترابطة التي تختزل إلى A_{2k} = 4A_{2k-2} - A_{2k-4}.

الخطوة 1: الحالتان الأساسيتان هما \( A_0 = 1 \) و\( A_2 = 3 \).

الخطوة 2: باستعمال التراجع \( A_{2k} = 4A_{2k-2} - A_{2k-4} \) نحسب الحدود المتتالية.

الخطوة 3: نحصل على \( A_{0} = 1, A_{2} = 3, A_{4} = 11, A_{6} = 41 \) ومنه \( A_{6} = 41 \).

en.question: In an Intermediate Olympiad tiling recurrence problem, how many ways can a \( 3 \times 8 \) grid be completely tiled with \( 1 \times 2 \) dominoes?
en.hint: Let \( A_{2k} \) be full tilings of \( 3 \times 2k \); eliminating corner-missing states yields \( A_{2k} = 4A_{2k-2} - A_{2k-4} \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Use coupled state recurrences A_{2k} = 3 A_{2k-2} + 2 B_{2k-3}, which reduces to A_{2k} = 4 A_{2k-2} - A_{2k-4}.

Step 1: For \( 3 \times 2k \) boards, base cases are \( A_0 = 1 \) and \( A_2 = 3 \).

Step 2: Coupling full columns \( A_{2k} \) and protruding-domino states gives the recurrence \( A_{2k} = 4A_{2k-2} - A_{2k-4} \).

Step 3: Computing sequentially gives \( A_{0} = 1, A_{2} = 3, A_{4} = 11, A_{6} = 41, A_{8} = 153 \), so \( A_{8} = 153 \).

✅ Quick Check: Notice \( A_{8} = 153 > 3^{4} = 81 \) because dominoes can straddle the boundaries between \( 3 \times 2 \) blocks.

en.question: How many binary strings of length \( 6 \) do not contain three consecutive ones (\( \text{"111"} \))?
en.hint: Partition valid strings by their prefix \( \text{"0"} \), \( \text{"10"} \), or \( \text{"110"} \) to get \( a_n = a_{n-1} + a_{n-2} + a_{n-3} \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Group valid strings by the position of the first zero to obtain the Tribonacci recurrence a_n = a_{n-1} + a_{n-2} + a_{n-3}.

Step 1: Base values are \( a_1 = 2 \), \( a_2 = 4 \), and \( a_3 = 7 \) (all \( 2^3 = 8 \) strings except \( 111 \)).

Step 2: Any valid string of length \( k \ge 4 \) starts with \( 0 \), \( 10 \), or \( 110 \), so \( a_k = a_{k-1} + a_{k-2} + a_{k-3} \).

Step 3: Generating terms up to \( k = 6 \) yields \( 2, 4, 7, 13, 24, 44 \), so \( a_{6} = 44 \).

✅ Quick Check: Check: \( 24 + 13 + 7 = 44 \).

ar.hint: صنّف السلاسل الصالحة حسب بدايتها \( \text{"0"} \) أو \( \text{"10"} \) أو \( \text{"110"} \) لتحصل على \( a_n = a_{n-1} + a_{n-2} + a_{n-3} \).
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نصنّف السلاسل الصالحة حسب موضع أول صفر فنحصل على علاقة تريبوناتشي التراجعية.

الخطوة 1: القيم الابتدائية هي \( a_1 = 2 \) و\( a_2 = 4 \) و\( a_3 = 7 \).

الخطوة 2: كل سلسلة صالحة تبدأ بـ \( 0 \) أو \( 10 \) أو \( 110 \) ومنه \( a_k = a_{k-1} + a_{k-2} + a_{k-3} \).

الخطوة 3: بحساب الحدود متتالية نجد \( a_{6} = 44 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: التحقق: \( 24 + 13 + 7 = 44 \).

en.question: A tree \( T \) has \( 4 \) internal vertices of degree \( 3 \), \( 3 \) internal vertices of degree \( 4 \), and all remaining vertices are leaves (degree \( 1 \)). How many leaves does \( T \) have?
en.hint: In a tree with \( L \) leaves, \( |V| = L + 7 \) and \( 2(|V| - 1) = L + 24 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Use the tree degree identity L = 2 + sum_{internal} (deg(v) - 2).

Step 1: Let \( L \) be the number of leaves. Then \( |V| = L + 7 \) and \( |E| = |V| - 1 = L + 6 \).

Step 2: By the Handshaking Lemma, \( L + 4\cdot3 + 3\cdot4 = 2(L + 6) \).

Step 3: Solving for \( L \) gives \( L = 2 + 4(3 - 2) + 3(4 - 2) = 12 \).

✅ Quick Check: With \( L = 12 \), \( |V| = 19 \), \( |E| = 18 \), and \( \sum \deg = 36 \).

💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نستعمل متطابقة درجات الشجرة L = 2 + sum (deg(v) - 2) على الرؤوس الداخلية.

الخطوة 1: ليكن \( L \) عدد الأوراق؛ إذن عدد الرؤوس \( |V| = L + 8 \) وعدد الأضلاع \( |V| - 1 \).

الخطوة 2: من توطئة المصافحة: \( L + 28 = 2(L + 7) \).

الخطوة 3: بحل المعادلة نجد \( L = 2 + 6(3-2) + 2(5-2) = 14 \).

en.question: A tree \( T \) has \( 3 \) internal vertices of degree \( 4 \), \( 4 \) internal vertices of degree \( 5 \), and all remaining vertices are leaves (degree \( 1 \)). How many leaves does \( T \) have?
en.hint: In a tree with \( L \) leaves, \( |V| = L + 7 \) and \( 2(|V| - 1) = L + 32 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Use the tree degree identity L = 2 + sum_{internal} (deg(v) - 2).

Step 1: Let \( L \) be the number of leaves. Then \( |V| = L + 7 \) and \( |E| = |V| - 1 = L + 6 \).

Step 2: By the Handshaking Lemma, \( L + 3\cdot4 + 4\cdot5 = 2(L + 6) \).

Step 3: Solving for \( L \) gives \( L = 2 + 3(4 - 2) + 4(5 - 2) = 20 \).

✅ Quick Check: With \( L = 20 \), \( |V| = 27 \), \( |E| = 26 \), and \( \sum \deg = 52 \).

ar.question: بموجب مبرهنة مانتل، ما أكبر عدد ممكن من الأضلاع في بيان بسيط يحتوي على \( 16 \) رأساً ولا يحتوي على أي مثلث (\( K_3 \))؟
ar.hint: بموجب مبرهنة مانتل، يتحقق الحد الأقصى في البيان الثنائي الكامل المتوازن \( K_{8, 8} \).
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نطبق مبرهنة مانتل التي تنص على أن أكبر عدد أضلاع في بيان خالٍ من المثلثات هو floor(n^2 / 4).

الخطوة 1: بموجب مبرهنة مانتل لا يتجاوز عدد الأضلاع \( \lfloor n^2 / 4 \rfloor \).

الخطوة 2: يتحقق هذا الحد في البيان الثنائي الكامل المتوازن \( K_{8, 8} \).

الخطوة 3: بحساب الجداء نجد \( 8 \times 8 = 64 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: البيان الثنائي خالٍ تماماً من الدورات الفردية وبالتالي لا يحوي أي مثلث.

en.question: In an Intermediate Olympiad extremal graph problem, what is the minimum number of edges that guarantees any simple graph on \( 10 \) vertices is connected?
en.hint: The most edges a disconnected graph on \( 10 \) vertices can have occurs in \( K_{9} \sqcup K_1 \), which has \( \binom{9}{2} \) edges.
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Add 1 to the maximum edge count C(n - 1, 2) of a disconnected n-vertex graph.

Step 1: A disconnected graph on \( 10 \) vertices with parts of sizes \( k \) and \( 10 - k \) has at most \( \binom{k}{2} + \binom{10 - k}{2} \) edges.

Step 2: By convexity, this is maximized at \( k = 1 \): \( K_{9} \sqcup K_1 \) has \( \binom{9}{2} = 36 \) edges and is still disconnected.

Step 3: Adding one more edge forces connectivity: \( 36 + 1 = 37 \).

✅ Quick Check: While \( 9 \) edges suffice to build one specific tree, \( 37 \) edges are required to guarantee connectivity for every simple graph.

en.question: A pile contains \( 100 \) stones. Two players alternate turns removing between \( 1 \) and \( 6 \) stones inclusive; the player who takes the last stone wins. How many stones must the first player remove on the opening turn to guarantee a win?
en.hint: Multiples of \( 7 \) are losing positions; reduce \( 100 \) modulo \( 7 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Maintain the modulo (m + 1) invariant by reducing the pile to a multiple of m + 1 after every move.

Step 1: Whenever the opponent removes \( k \in \{1, \dots, 6\} \) stones, the first player can remove \( 7 - k \) stones to preserve multiples of \( 7 \).

Step 2: Divide \( 100 \) by \( 7 \): \( 100 = 14 \cdot 7 + 2 \).

Step 3: Removing \( 2 \) stones leaves a multiple of \( 7 \), securing a winning strategy.

✅ Quick Check: Since \( 1 \le 2 \le 6 \), removing \( 2 \) stones is a legal and unique winning opening move.

ar.question: كومة تحتوي على \( 100 \) حجراً. يتناوب لاعبان على سحب عدد من الأحجار يتراوح بين \( 1 \) و\( 6 \) في كل دور، والفائز هو من يسحب الحجر الأخير. كم حجراً يجب أن يسحب اللاعب الأول في نقالته الأولى ليضمن الفوز؟
ar.hint: مضاعفات العدد \( 7 \) هي مواقع خاسرة؛ احسب باقي قسمة \( 100 \) على \( 7 \).
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نحافظ على اللامتغير معيار (m + 1) بترك مضاعف للعدد (m + 1) بعد كل دور.

الخطوة 1: المواقع التي تقبل القسمة على \( 7 \) مواقع خاسرة لمن عليه الدور.

الخطوة 2: نقسم \( 100 \) على \( 7 \): \( 100 = 14 \times 7 + 2 \).

الخطوة 3: لذلك يسحب اللاعب الأول \( 2 \) أحجار ليترك لمنافسه مضاعفاً للعدد \( 7 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: النقلة \( 2 \) قانونية وتقع ضمن المدى المسموح \( [1, 6] \).

ar.question: كومة تحتوي على \( 248 \) حجراً. يتناوب لاعبان على سحب عدد من الأحجار يتراوح بين \( 1 \) و\( 10 \) في كل دور، والفائز هو من يسحب الحجر الأخير. كم حجراً يجب أن يسحب اللاعب الأول في نقالته الأولى ليضمن الفوز؟
ar.hint: مضاعفات العدد \( 11 \) هي مواقع خاسرة؛ احسب باقي قسمة \( 248 \) على \( 11 \).
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نحافظ على اللامتغير معيار (m + 1) بترك مضاعف للعدد (m + 1) بعد كل دور.

الخطوة 1: المواقع التي تقبل القسمة على \( 11 \) مواقع خاسرة لمن عليه الدور.

الخطوة 2: نقسم \( 248 \) على \( 11 \): \( 248 = 22 \times 11 + 6 \).

الخطوة 3: لذلك يسحب اللاعب الأول \( 6 \) أحجار ليترك لمنافسه مضاعفاً للعدد \( 11 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: النقلة \( 6 \) قانونية وتقع ضمن المدى المسموح \( [1, 10] \).

en.question: A pile contains \( 302 \) stones. Two players alternate turns removing between \( 1 \) and \( 12 \) stones inclusive; the player who takes the last stone wins. How many stones must the first player remove on the opening turn to guarantee a win?
en.hint: Multiples of \( 13 \) are losing positions; reduce \( 302 \) modulo \( 13 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Maintain the modulo (m + 1) invariant by reducing the pile to a multiple of m + 1 after every move.

Step 1: Whenever the opponent removes \( k \in \{1, \dots, 12\} \) stones, the first player can remove \( 13 - k \) stones to preserve multiples of \( 13 \).

Step 2: Divide \( 302 \) by \( 13 \): \( 302 = 23 \cdot 13 + 3 \).

Step 3: Removing \( 3 \) stones leaves a multiple of \( 13 \), securing a winning strategy.

✅ Quick Check: Since \( 1 \le 3 \le 12 \), removing \( 3 \) stones is a legal and unique winning opening move.

en.question: The integers \( 1, 2, \dots, 20 \) are written on a blackboard. Each step, two numbers \( a \) and \( b \) are erased and replaced by \( a + b - 3 \). After \( 19 \) steps, only one number remains. What is this final number?
en.hint: Notice that \( (a + b - 3) - 3 = (a - 3) + (b - 3) \), so \( \sum (x_i - 3) \) is invariant!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Track the invariant shifted sum sum(x_i - c), or note each of the n - 1 merges subtracts c from the total sum.

Step 1: Initial sum of the \( 20 \) numbers is \( \frac{20(20 + 1)}{2} = 210 \).

Step 2: Each operation decreases the count of numbers by \( 1 \) and decreases the total sum by exactly \( 3 \).

Step 3: After \( 19 \) operations, the single remaining number is \( 210 - 19 \cdot 3 = 153 \).

✅ Quick Check: Shifted invariant check: \( X - 3 = \sum_{k=1}^{20} (k - 3) = 150 \), giving \( X = 153 \).

ar.question: كُتبت الأعداد الصحيحة \( 1, 2, \dots, 20 \) على سبورة. في كل خطوة يُمسح عددان \( a \) و\( b \) ويُكتب مكانهما العدد \( a + b - 3 \). بعد \( 19 \) خطوة يبقى عدد واحد فقط. ما قيمة هذا العدد النهائي؟
ar.hint: لاحظ أن \( (a + b - 3) - 3 = (a - 3) + (b - 3) \)، أي أن المجموع \( \sum (x_i - 3) \) لامتغير!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نتتبع اللامتغير لمجموع الأعداد المزاحة، حيث تنقص كل خطوة المجموع الكلي بمقدار ثابت c.

الخطوة 1: المجموع الابتدائي للأعداد هو \( \frac{20(21)}{2} = 210 \).

الخطوة 2: في كل خطوة من الخطوات البالغ عددها \( 19 \) ينقص المجموع الكلي بمقدار \( 3 \) بالضبط.

الخطوة 3: إذن العدد الوحيد المتبقي في النهاية هو \( 210 - 19 \times 3 = 153 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: التحقق باللامتغير المزاح يؤكد أن \( X = 153 \) بغض النظر عن ترتيب الاختيار.

en.question: The integers \( 1, 2, \dots, 30 \) are written on a blackboard. Each step, two numbers \( a \) and \( b \) are erased and replaced by \( a + b - 5 \). After \( 29 \) steps, only one number remains. What is this final number?
en.hint: Notice that \( (a + b - 5) - 5 = (a - 5) + (b - 5) \), so \( \sum (x_i - 5) \) is invariant!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Track the invariant shifted sum sum(x_i - c), or note each of the n - 1 merges subtracts c from the total sum.

Step 1: Initial sum of the \( 30 \) numbers is \( \frac{30(30 + 1)}{2} = 465 \).

Step 2: Each operation decreases the count of numbers by \( 1 \) and decreases the total sum by exactly \( 5 \).

Step 3: After \( 29 \) operations, the single remaining number is \( 465 - 29 \cdot 5 = 320 \).

✅ Quick Check: Shifted invariant check: \( X - 5 = \sum_{k=1}^{30} (k - 5) = 315 \), giving \( X = 320 \).

ar.hint: لاحظ أن \( (a + b - 5) - 5 = (a - 5) + (b - 5) \)، أي أن المجموع \( \sum (x_i - 5) \) لامتغير!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نتتبع اللامتغير لمجموع الأعداد المزاحة، حيث تنقص كل خطوة المجموع الكلي بمقدار ثابت c.

الخطوة 1: المجموع الابتدائي للأعداد هو \( \frac{30(31)}{2} = 465 \).

الخطوة 3: إذن العدد الوحيد المتبقي في النهاية هو \( 465 - 29 \times 5 = 320 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: التحقق باللامتغير المزاح يؤكد أن \( X = 320 \) بغض النظر عن ترتيب الاختيار.

en.question: In a three-pile game of Nim with pile sizes \( (6, 10, 15) \), how many stones must the first player remove from the pile of size \( 15 \) to leave a balanced XOR-sum \( 0 \) position?
en.hint: By Bouton's theorem, reduce the third pile to \( 6 \oplus 10 = 12 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Compute the binary XOR sum of the first two piles and subtract it from the third pile.

Step 1: By Bouton's theorem for Nim, a position is losing for the next player if and only if its Nim-sum (bitwise XOR) is \( 0 \).

Step 2: Compute the XOR of the first two piles in binary: \( 6 \oplus 10 = 12 \).

Step 3: To reduce the third pile from \( 15 \) to \( 12 \), remove \( 15 - 12 = 3 \) stones.

✅ Quick Check: After removing \( 3 \) stones, the piles are \( (6, 10, 12) \) with XOR-sum \( 6 \oplus 10 \oplus 12 = 0 \).

ar.question: في لعبة نيم المكونة من ثلاث أكوام أحجامها \( (6, 10, 15) \)، كم حجراً يجب أن يسحب اللاعب الأول من الكومة ذات الحجم \( 15 \) ليترك موقعاً متوازناً مجموعه الثنائي الحصري (XOR) يساوي \( 0 \)؟
ar.hint: بموجب مبرهنة بوتون، اختزل الكومة الثالثة إلى القيمة \( 6 \oplus 10 = 12 \).
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نحسب المجموع الثنائي الحصري (XOR) للكومتين الأوليين ثم نطرحه من حجم الكومة الثالثة.

الخطوة 1: بموجب مبرهنة بوتون في لعبة نيم، يكون الموقع متوازناً إذا وفقط إذا كان مجموع XOR للأكوام يساوي \( 0 \).

الخطوة 2: نحسب في النظام الثنائي: \( 6 \oplus 10 = 12 \).

الخطوة 3: لتقليص الكومة الثالثة من \( 15 \) إلى \( 12 \) نسحب \( 15 - 12 = 3 \) حجراً.

✅ التحقق من الحل: بعد السحب تصبح الأحجام \( (6, 10, 12) \) ومجموعها الحصري \( 0 \).

en.question: The integers \( 1, 2, \dots, 5 \) are written on a board. Repeatedly, two numbers \( a, b \) are erased and replaced by \( ab + a + b \) until one number remains. What is the final number?
en.hint: Factor \( (ab + a + b) + 1 = (a + 1)(b + 1) \), showing that \( \prod (x_i + 1) \) is an invariant!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Use the identity (ab + a + b) + 1 = (a + 1)(b + 1) so the product of (x_i + 1) remains invariant.

Step 1: Observe the algebraic identity \( (ab + a + b) + 1 = (a + 1)(b + 1) \).

Step 2: Thus the product \( \prod (x_i + 1) \) over all numbers on the board is invariant under every replacement.

Step 3: Initially \( \prod_{k=1}^{5} (k + 1) = 2 \cdot 3 \cdots 6 = 6! = 720 \), so the final number \( X \) satisfies \( X + 1 = 720 \), giving \( X = 719 \).

✅ Quick Check: Regardless of the order in which pairs are merged, \( X = 6! - 1 = 719 \).

ar.question: كُتبت الأعداد \( 1, 2, \dots, 5 \) على لوح. في كل خطوة يُمسح عددان \( a, b \) ويُكتب مكانهما \( ab + a + b \) حتى يبقى عدد واحد فقط. ما قيمة هذا العدد النهائي؟
ar.hint: حلّل المقدار \( (ab + a + b) + 1 = (a + 1)(b + 1) \) لتستنتج أن الجداء \( \prod (x_i + 1) \) لامتغير!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نستعمل المتطابقة (ab + a + b) + 1 = (a + 1)(b + 1) فيبقى جداء (x_i + 1) ثابتاً لا يتغير.

الخطوة 1: نلاحظ المتطابقة الجبرية \( (ab + a + b) + 1 = (a + 1)(b + 1) \).

الخطوة 2: إذن الجداء \( \prod (x_i + 1) \) لامتغير في كل خطوة.

الخطوة 3: في البداية يساوي الجداء \( 2 \times 3 \times \cdots \times 6 = 6! = 720 \)، فيكون العدد النهائي \( X = 720 - 1 = 719 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: قيمة العدد النهائي \( 719 \) ثابتة ومستقلة تماماً عن ترتيب الدمج.

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad prime divisor problem, let \( p \) be the smallest prime factor of \( (2^{5} - 1)/(2 - 1) \). Find \( p \).
en.hint: Every prime factor \( p \) not dividing \( 2-1 \) satisfies \( \operatorname{ord}_p(2) = 5 \), so \( p \equiv 1 \pmod{5} \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: By multiplicative orders, any prime dividing (a^q - 1)/(a - 1) for prime q satisfies p = 1 (mod q).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad sum-of-squares divisibility problem, suppose \( 81 = 3^4 \) divides \( x^2 + y^2 \) for positive integers \( x,y \). What is the minimum possible value of \( x + y \)?
en.hint: Repeatedly applying the \( p \equiv 3 \pmod 4 \) lemma shows \( 3^2 = 9 \) must divide both \( x \) and \( y \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Since v_3(x^2 + y^2) = 2 min(v_3(x), v_3(y)), divisibility by 3^4 forces 9 | x and 9 | y.

Step 1: Thus \( x \ge 9 \) and \( y \ge 9 \), giving minimum sum \( 9 + 9 = 18 \).

✅ Quick Check: At \( x=y=9 \), \( x^2+y^2=162 = 2 \times 81 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad sum-of-squares divisibility problem, suppose \( p = 19 \equiv 3 \pmod 4 \) divides \( x^2 + y^2 \) for positive integers \( x,y \). What is the minimum possible value of \( x + y \)?
en.hint: Because \( -1 \) is a quadratic non-residue modulo \( 19 \equiv 3 \pmod 4 \), \( 19 \mid (x^2+y^2) \) forces \( 19 \mid x \) and \( 19 \mid y \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: By Fermat's 4k+3 lemma, p | x^2 + y^2 implies p | x and p | y.

Step 1: Since \( x, y \ge 1 \) are multiples of \( 19 \), the minimum is \( x = y = 19 \), giving \( x + y = 38 \) (unless False, where we require \( x^2+y^2 \) divisible by \( 81 \) so \( 9 \mid x,y \) and \( x+y=18 \)).

✅ Quick Check: Minimum sum verified: \( 38 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Jacobi two-square theorem problem, how many ordered pairs of integers \( (x, y) \in \mathbb{{Z}}^2 \) satisfy \( x^2 + y^2 = 65 \)?
en.hint: By Jacobi's two-square theorem, \( r_2(N) = 4(d_1(N) - d_3(N)) \), where \( d_1, d_3 \) count divisors congruent to \( 1, 3 \pmod 4 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: For N composed only of primes p = 1 (mod 4), r_2(N) = 4 * tau(N).

Step 1: Since all prime factors of \( 65 \) are \( \equiv 1 \pmod 4 \), \( r_2(65) = 4 \tau(65) = 16 \).

✅ Quick Check: Direct lattice search confirms \( 16 \) integer pairs.

en.hint: Substitute \( a=2 \) and \( b=8 \) into \( (a^2+b^2)/(ab+1) \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Every positive integer ratio k = (a^2 + b^2)/(ab + 1) is a perfect square generated from (t, t^3).

ar.hint: عوّض \( a=2 \) و\( b=8 \) في الكسر \( (a^2+b^2)/(ab+1) \).
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: كل خارج قسمة صحيح موجب k = (a^2 + b^2)/(ab + 1) هو مربع كامل يتولد من (t, t^3).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Vieta root-flipping step on \( x^2 - 3xy + y^2 = 1 \), starting from the solution \( (x, y) = (1, 3) \), find the larger second root \( x' = ky - x \) when \( y = 3 \) is held fixed.
en.hint: By Vieta's sum of roots for \( x^2 - (3y)x + (y^2-1) = 0 \), the two roots satisfy \( x + x' = 3y \).

en.question: In the Senior Olympiad symmetric triple equation \( a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = 3abc \), given \( a = 1 \) and \( b = 1 \), find the larger positive integer solution \( c \).
en.hint: Treat the equation as a quadratic \( c^2 - (3ab)c + (a^2+b^2) = 0 \) and factor or use Vieta root jumping.
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: As a quadratic in c, c^2 - 3ab c + (a^2 + b^2) = 0 has roots summing to 3ab.

Step 1: Substitute \( a=1, b=1 \): \( c^2 - 3c + 2 = 0 \), whose larger integer root is \( c = 2 \).

✅ Quick Check: Verified: \( 1^2 + 1^2 + 2^2 = 6 = 3(1)(1)(2) \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad cyclotomic evaluation task, compute the numerical value of \( \Phi_{5}(2) \).

en.hint: Apply the \( 4 \)th roots of unity filter to \( (1+x)^{12} \).

Step 1: Summing \( \binom{12}{j} \) over \( j \equiv 0 \pmod{4} \) yields \( 992 \).

✅ Quick Check: Direct binomial summation confirms \( 992 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Chebyshev polynomial problem, let \( T_n(x) \) satisfy \( T_n(\cos\theta) = \cos(n\theta) \). Evaluate \( T_{3}(2) \).
en.hint: Use the Chebyshev recurrence \( T_{{n+1}}(x) = 2x T_n(x) - T_{{n-1}}(x) \) starting from \( T_0(x)=1, T_1(x)=x \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind obey T_{n+1}(x) = 2x T_n(x) - T_{n-1}(x).

Step 1: Iterating from \( T_0(2)=1 \) and \( T_1(2)=2 \) up to \( n=3 \) gives \( T_{3}(2) = 26 \).

✅ Quick Check: Verified via Chebyshev recurrence: \( 26 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Cauchy functional equation problem, let \( f: \mathbb{{Q}} \to \mathbb{{Q}} \) satisfy \( f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y) \) for all \( x, y \in \mathbb{{Q}} \) and \( f(1) = 7 \). Find \( f(12) \).
en.hint: By induction on rationals, Cauchy's additive equation gives \( f(x) = f(1)x \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: On Q, additivity forces f(q) = q * f(1) for every rational q.

Step 1: Therefore \( f(12) = 7 \times 12 = 84 \).

✅ Quick Check: Verified linear solution: \( 84 \).

en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: On Q, additivity forces f(q) = q * f(1) for every rational q.

Step 1: Therefore \( f(8) = 16 \times 8 = 128 \).

✅ Quick Check: Verified linear solution: \( 128 \).

💡 الفكرة الأساسية: على الأعداد الناطقة، الجمعية تفرض f(q) = q * f(1).

الخطوة 1: إذن \( f(8) = 16 \times 8 = 128 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تم التحقق من الحل الخطي: \( 128 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad involution functional equation, suppose \( f: \mathbb{{R}} \to \mathbb{{R}} \) satisfies \( 2f(x) + f(10 - x) = 2x + 38 \) for all real \( x \). Compute \( f(4) \).
en.hint: Substitute \( x = 4 \) and \( x = 6 \) to form a \( 2 \times 2 \) linear system in \( f(4) \) and \( f(6) \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Pairing x and (b - x) eliminates f(b - x) via 2*Eq(x) - Eq(b - x).

Step 1: At \( x=4 \), \( 2f(4)+f(6)=46 \); at \( x=6 \), \( 2f(6)+f(4)=50 \). Solving gives \( f(4) = 14 \).

✅ Quick Check: System verified: \( 3f(4) = 42 \implies f(4) = 14 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad polynomial functional equation, let \( P(x) \) be a non-constant polynomial satisfying \( P(x)P(y) = P(xy) + P(x) + P(y) - 2 \) with \( P(2) = 9 \) and degree \( 3 \). Confirm the value of \( P(2) \).
en.hint: Rewrite the equation as \( (P(x)-1)(P(y)-1) = P(xy)-1 \), so \( Q(x) = P(x)-1 \) is multiplicative and thus \( Q(x) = x^{3} \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Setting Q(x) = P(x) - 1 gives Q(x)Q(y) = Q(xy), whose degree-k polynomial solution is Q(x) = x^k.

Step 1: Hence \( P(x) = x^{3} + 1 \), so \( P(2) = 2^{3} + 1 = 9 \).

✅ Quick Check: Verified polynomial identity at \( x=2 \): \( 9 \).

✅ Quick Check: Exponent verified: \( 8 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad quadratic Chebyshev recurrence, let \( x_0 = 2 \) and \( x_{{n+1}} = 2x_n^2 - 1 \) for \( n \ge 0 \). Compute \( x_{2} \).
en.hint: Iterate \( x \mapsto 2x^2 - 1 \) \( 2 \) time(s) starting from \( x_0 = 2 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: The map x -> 2x^2 - 1 corresponds to T_2(x), so x_n = T_{2^n}(x_0).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad rational recurrence problem, let \( x_0 = 2 \) and \( x_{{n+1}} = \frac{{x_n + 3}}{{x_n - 1}} \) for \( n \ge 0 \). Evaluate \( x_{100} \).
en.hint: Compute \( x_2 \) in terms of \( x_0 \) to discover that the fractional linear map is an involution of period \( 2 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: The Mobius transformation f(x) = (x + 3)/(x - 1) satisfies f(f(x)) = x, so x_{2k} = x_0.

Step 1: Since \( f(f(x)) = \frac{(x+3)/(x-1)+3}{(x+3)/(x-1)-1} = \frac{4x}{4} = x \) and \( 100 \) is even, \( x_{100} = x_0 = 2 \).

✅ Quick Check: Period-2 invariance verified: \( 2 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad rational recurrence problem, let \( x_0 = 7 \) and \( x_{{n+1}} = \frac{{x_n + 3}}{{x_n - 1}} \) for \( n \ge 0 \). Evaluate \( x_{600} \).
en.hint: Compute \( x_2 \) in terms of \( x_0 \) to discover that the fractional linear map is an involution of period \( 2 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: The Mobius transformation f(x) = (x + 3)/(x - 1) satisfies f(f(x)) = x, so x_{2k} = x_0.

Step 1: Since \( f(f(x)) = \frac{(x+3)/(x-1)+3}{(x+3)/(x-1)-1} = \frac{4x}{4} = x \) and \( 600 \) is even, \( x_{600} = x_0 = 7 \).

✅ Quick Check: Period-2 invariance verified: \( 7 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Power Mean (QM-AM) problem, if \( 3 \) positive reals satisfy \( x_1 + \dots + x_{3} = 6 \), find the minimum possible value of \( x_1^2 + \dots + x_{3}^2 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad three-bracket Hölder inequality problem, positive reals \( a_i, b_i, c_i \) (\( 1 \le i \le 3 \)) satisfy \( a_i b_i c_i = 2 \) for each \( i \). Find the minimum value of \( \left(\sum a_i^3\right)\left(\sum b_i^3\right)\left(\sum c_i^3\right) \).
en.hint: By Hölder's inequality, \( (\sum a_i^3)(\sum b_i^3)(\sum c_i^3) \ge (\sum a_i b_i c_i)^3 \).

💡 Key Idea: Three-bracket Holder inequality bounds the product of cubic sums from below by (sum a_i b_i c_i)^3.

Step 1: Here \( \sum_{i=1}^{3} a_i b_i c_i = 3 \times 2 = 6 \), so the minimum is \( 6^3 = 216 \).

✅ Quick Check: Equality holds when all variables are equal: \( 216 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad three-bracket Hölder inequality problem, positive reals \( a_i, b_i, c_i \) (\( 1 \le i \le 2 \)) satisfy \( a_i b_i c_i = 5 \) for each \( i \). Find the minimum value of \( \left(\sum a_i^3\right)\left(\sum b_i^3\right)\left(\sum c_i^3\right) \).
en.hint: By Hölder's inequality, \( (\sum a_i^3)(\sum b_i^3)(\sum c_i^3) \ge (\sum a_i b_i c_i)^3 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Three-bracket Holder inequality bounds the product of cubic sums from below by (sum a_i b_i c_i)^3.

Step 1: Here \( \sum_{i=1}^{2} a_i b_i c_i = 2 \times 5 = 10 \), so the minimum is \( 10^3 = 1000 \).

✅ Quick Check: Equality holds when all variables are equal: \( 1000 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad radical Hölder inequality problem, positive reals \( a, b, c \) satisfy \( a + b + c = 3 \). Find the minimum possible value of \( 2\left(\frac{{a}}{{\sqrt{{2b+2c}}}} + \frac{{b}}{{\sqrt{{2c+2a}}}} + \frac{{c}}{{\sqrt{{2a+2b}}}}\right) \).
en.hint: Apply Hölder's inequality \( \left(\sum \frac{{a}}{{\sqrt{{2b+2c}}}}\right)^2 \left(\sum a(2b+2c)\right) \ge (a+b+c)^3 \) and use \( \sum ab \le (a+b+c)^2/3 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: By Holder's inequality, (sum a/sqrt(2b+2c))^2 * (4 sum ab) >= (a+b+c)^3.

Step 1: At equality \( a = b = c = 1 \), each radical denominator is \( \sqrt{4 \cdot 1} = 2 \), giving minimum \( 2 \times 3 \times \frac{1}{2} = 3 \).

✅ Quick Check: Symmetric equality point confirms \( 3 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Muirhead majorization problem, since \( (3,0,0) \succ (2,1,0) \succ (1,1,1) \), find the minimum value of the symmetric sum \( \sum_{{sym}} a^2 b \) for positive reals \( a, b, c \) satisfying \( abc = 8 \).
en.hint: By Muirhead's inequality, \( \sum_{{sym}} a^2 b \ge \sum_{{sym}} a b c = 6abc \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: The 6-term symmetric sum sum_{sym} a^2 b majorizes sum_{sym} a^1 b^1 c^1 = 6abc.

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Jensen convexity problem, for \( 3 \) positive reals satisfying \( x_1 + \dots + x_{3} = 6 \), find the minimum value of \( x_1^3 + \dots + x_{3}^3 \).
en.hint: Since \( f(x) = x^3 \) is strictly convex on \( (0, \infty) \), Jensen's inequality gives \( \sum x_i^3 \ge 3 (\bar{x})^3 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: By Jensen's inequality for convex f(x) = x^3, sum f(x_i) >= n f((sum x_i)/n).

Step 1: The mean is \( \bar{x} = 6/3 = 2 \), so the minimum is \( 3 \times 2^3 = 24 \).

✅ Quick Check: Attained at \( x_i = 2 \): \( 24 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Jensen convexity problem, for \( 5 \) positive reals satisfying \( x_1 + \dots + x_{5} = 10 \), find the minimum value of \( x_1^3 + \dots + x_{5}^3 \).
en.hint: Since \( f(x) = x^3 \) is strictly convex on \( (0, \infty) \), Jensen's inequality gives \( \sum x_i^3 \ge 5 (\bar{x})^3 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: By Jensen's inequality for convex f(x) = x^3, sum f(x_i) >= n f((sum x_i)/n).

Step 1: The mean is \( \bar{x} = 10/5 = 2 \), so the minimum is \( 5 \times 2^3 = 40 \).

✅ Quick Check: Attained at \( x_i = 2 \): \( 40 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad constrained extremal problem on the sphere \( x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 9 \), find the maximum possible value of \( 1x + 2y + 2z \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: On x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = R^2, the maximum of c_1 x + c_2 y + c_3 z is R * sqrt(c_1^2 + c_2^2 + c_3^2).

Step 1: Since \( 1^2+2^2+2^2 = 9 \) and \( x^2+y^2+z^2 = 9 \), the maximum is \( \sqrt{9 \times 9} = 9 \).

✅ Quick Check: Attained at \( (x,y,z) = (1,2,2) \): \( 9 \).

en.hint: By the Incenter-Excenter Lemma, \( M \) is the circumcenter of \( B I C I_A \) with diameter \( II_A \), so \( MI = MI_A = MB \).

ar.hint: وفق توطئة المركز الداخلي والخارجي، النقطة \( M \) هي مركز الدائرة المارة بالنقاط \( B, I, C, I_A \) وقطرها \( II_A \)، لذا \( MI = MI_A = MB \).
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: حسب توطئة المركز الداخلي والخارجي، MB = MC = MI = MI_A، والنقطة M منتصف القطر II_A.

الخطوة 1: إذن \( II_A = 2 \cdot MB = 2 \times 7 = 14 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تم التحقق من طول القطر: \( 14 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Incenter-Excenter Lemma problem, let \( M \) be the midpoint of arc \( BC \) (not containing \( A \)) of the circumcircle of \( \triangle ABC \), with incenter \( I \) and \( A \)-excenter \( I_A \). If \( MB = 9 \), find the segment length \( II_A \).
en.hint: By the Incenter-Excenter Lemma, \( M \) is the circumcenter of \( B I C I_A \) with diameter \( II_A \), so \( MI = MI_A = MB \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: By the Incenter-Excenter Lemma (Fact 5), MB = MC = MI = MI_A, and M is the midpoint of diameter II_A.

Step 1: Therefore \( II_A = 2 \cdot MB = 2 \times 9 = 18 \).

✅ Quick Check: Diameter length verified: \( 18 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Incenter-Excenter Lemma problem, let \( M \) be the midpoint of arc \( BC \) (not containing \( A \)) of the circumcircle of \( \triangle ABC \), with incenter \( I \) and \( A \)-excenter \( I_A \). If \( MB = 15 \), find the segment length \( II_A \).
en.hint: By the Incenter-Excenter Lemma, \( M \) is the circumcenter of \( B I C I_A \) with diameter \( II_A \), so \( MI = MI_A = MB \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: By the Incenter-Excenter Lemma (Fact 5), MB = MC = MI = MI_A, and M is the midpoint of diameter II_A.

Step 1: Therefore \( II_A = 2 \cdot MB = 2 \times 15 = 30 \).

✅ Quick Check: Diameter length verified: \( 30 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Euler triangle distance problem, a triangle has circumradius \( R = 10 \) and inradius \( r = 3 \). Compute \( OI^2 \), the squared distance between circumcenter \( O \) and incenter \( I \).
en.hint: Apply Euler's formula \( OI^2 = R(R - 2r) \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Euler's theorem in triangle geometry states OI^2 = R^2 - 2Rr = R(R - 2r).

Step 1: Substitute \( R = 10 \) and \( r = 3 \): \( OI^2 = 10(10 - 2 \times 3) = 40 \).

✅ Quick Check: Euler distance squared verified: \( 40 \).

en.hint: By Steiner's theorem, the Simson line of \( P \) passes through the midpoint \( M \) of segment \( PH \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: The Steiner line is the image of the Simson line under homothety (P, 2) and passes through H, so M is the midpoint of PH.

Step 1: Therefore \( PH = 2 \cdot PM = 2 \times 5 = 10 \).

✅ Quick Check: Midpoint property verified: \( 10 \).

ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: الانعكاس الدائري يحقق العلاقة OP * OP' = R^2.

الخطوة 1: نحسب \( OP' = 30^2 / 20 = 45 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تم التحقق من جداء الانعكاس: \( 45 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad spiral similarity problem centered at \( S \), the spiral similarity mapping \( A \mapsto A' \) and \( B \mapsto B' \) satisfies \( SA = 6 \), \( SA' = 9 \), and \( AB = 12 \). Find \( A'B' \).
en.hint: A spiral similarity scales all segment lengths by the constant ratio \( k = SA' / SA \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Spiral similarity preserves ratios: A'B' / AB = SA' / SA.

Step 1: Thus \( A'B' = AB \cdot \frac{SA'}{SA} = 12 \times \frac{9}{6} = 18 \).

✅ Quick Check: Scale ratio confirmed: \( 18 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad circle inversion formula problem, a circle \( \omega \) of radius \( r = 2 \) has center at distance \( d = 7 \) from the inversion pole \( O \). Under inversion of radius \( R = 30 \), find the radius \( r' \) of the inverted circle \( \omega' \).
en.hint: Use the inverted-circle radius formula \( r' = \frac{{R^2 r}}{{|d^2 - r^2|}} \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Inverting the diametrically nearest and farthest points d - r and d + r gives 2r' = R^2/(d-r) - R^2/(d+r), so r' = R^2 r / (d^2 - r^2).

Step 1: Compute \( r' = \frac{30^2 \times 2}{7^2 - 2^2} = \frac{1800}{45} = 40 \).

✅ Quick Check: Inverted circle radius verified: \( 40 \).

en.hint: Square Sylvester's relation to obtain \( OH^2 = 9R^2 - (a^2 + b^2 + c^2) \).

✅ Quick Check: Euler-line squared distance verified: \( 25 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Pascal's Hexagon Theorem problem, the three opposite-side intersections of a cyclic hexagon are \( X(2,5) \), \( Y(4,9) \), and \( Z(6, k) \). Find \( k \).
en.hint: By Pascal's Theorem, \( X, Y, Z \) are collinear on the Pascal line, so the slopes of \( XY \) and \( XZ \) are equal.

💡 Key Idea: Pascal's Theorem guarantees that opposite sides of a cyclic hexagon meet in three collinear points.

Step 1: The slope of \( XY \) is \( (9-5)/(4-2) = 2 \), so \( k = 5 + 2(6-2) = 13 \).

✅ Quick Check: Pascal line collinearity verified: \( 13 \).

en.hint: By Pascal's Theorem, \( X, Y, Z \) are collinear on the Pascal line, so the slopes of \( XY \) and \( XZ \) are equal.

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad pole-polar reciprocity problem with respect to the circle \( x^2 + y^2 = 25 \), the polar line of pole \( P(3, 4) \) passes through \( Q(3, t) \). Find \( t \).
en.hint: The polar of \( P(3,4) \) with respect to \( x^2 + y^2 = 25 \) has equation \( 3x + 4y = 25 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: The polar of (x_0, y_0) with respect to x^2 + y^2 = R^2 is x_0 x + y_0 y = R^2.

✅ Quick Check: Polar incidence verified: \( 4 \).

en.hint: Use the orthocentric opposite-edge sum of squares invariant \( BD^2 = AB^2 + CD^2 - AC^2 \).

💡 Key Idea: In an orthocentric tetrahedron, the sum of squares of each pair of opposite edges is equal.

✅ Quick Check: Opposite edge length verified: \( 7 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad orthocentric tetrahedron problem, opposite edges are perpendicular so \( AB^2 + CD^2 = AC^2 + BD^2 = AD^2 + BC^2 \). Given \( AB = 1 \), \( CD = 12 \), and \( AC = 8 \), find \( BD \).
en.hint: Use the orthocentric opposite-edge sum of squares invariant \( BD^2 = AB^2 + CD^2 - AC^2 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: In an orthocentric tetrahedron, the sum of squares of each pair of opposite edges is equal.

Step 1: Here \( AB^2 + CD^2 = 1^2 + 12^2 = 145 \), so \( BD = \sqrt{145 - 8^2} = 9 \).

✅ Quick Check: Opposite edge length verified: \( 9 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad 3D geometry problem, an equifacial (dispisphenoid) tetrahedron is formed by four non-adjacent vertices of a rectangular box of dimensions \( 2 \times 2 \times 3 \). Compute \( 3V \), where \( V \) is the volume of the tetrahedron.
en.hint: Subtract the four congruent right corner tetrahedra (each of volume \( xyz/6 \)) from the box volume \( xyz \) to get \( V = xyz/3 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Inscribing an equifacial tetrahedron inside an x by y by z cuboid removes four corner pyramids of total volume 4(xyz/6) = 2xyz/3, leaving V = xyz/3.

Step 1: Thus \( 3V = 2 \times 2 \times 3 = 12 \).

✅ Quick Check: Cuboid embedding volume verified: \( 12 \).

en.hint: Subtract the four congruent right corner tetrahedra (each of volume \( xyz/6 \)) from the box volume \( xyz \) to get \( V = xyz/3 \).

💡 Key Idea: Inscribing an equifacial tetrahedron inside an x by y by z cuboid removes four corner pyramids of total volume 4(xyz/6) = 2xyz/3, leaving V = xyz/3.

en.hint: Decompose the tetrahedron into four pyramids from the incenter to obtain \( 3V = r(S_1 + S_2 + S_3 + S_4) \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Just as A = r s in 2D, a tetrahedron satisfies 3V = r * S where S is the sum of the four face areas.

Step 1: Compute \( r = \frac{3V}{S} = \frac{3 \times 40}{60} = 2 \).

✅ Quick Check: Insphere radius verified: \( 2 \).

ar.question: في مسألة الكرة الداخلة لرباعي الأوجه في الأولمبياد المتقدم، رباعي أوجه حجمه \( V = 240 \) ومساحته السطحية الكلية \( S = S_1 + S_2 + S_3 + S_4 = 120 \). أوجد نصف قطر الكرة الداخلة \( r \).
ar.hint: قسّم رباعي الأوجه إلى أربعة أهرامات رأسها مركز الكرة الداخلة لتحصل على \( 3V = r(S_1 + S_2 + S_3 + S_4) \).
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: بتجزئة رباعي الأوجه حول مركز الكرة الداخلة نجد أن 3V = r * S.

الخطوة 1: نحسب \( r = \frac{3 \times 240}{120} = 6 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تم التحقق من نصف قطر الكرة الداخلة: \( 6 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Fagnano's problem, an acute triangle \( \triangle ABC \) has area \( K = 30 \) and circumradius \( R = 5 \). Find the minimum perimeter of an inscribed triangle (achieved by the orthic triangle).
en.hint: The orthic triangle has minimum perimeter given by \( P_{{\min}} = \frac{{2K}}{{R}} \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: By reflection across the sides (Fagnano's theorem), the orthic triangle minimizes perimeter with P = 2K / R.

Step 1: Compute \( P_{\min} = \frac{2 \times 30}{5} = 12 \).

✅ Quick Check: Fagnano minimum perimeter verified: \( 12 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Fermat-Torricelli point problem, point \( F \) inside \( \triangle ABC \) satisfies \( \angle AFB = \angle BFC = \angle CFA = 120^\circ \). If \( FA = 3 \) and \( FB = 5 \), find the side length \( AB \).
en.hint: Apply the Law of Cosines in \( \triangle AFB \) with \( \cos 120^\circ = -1/2 \): \( AB^2 = FA^2 + FA \cdot FB + FB^2 \).

✅ Quick Check: Eisenstein triple verified: \( 7 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad isoperimetric inscribed-polygon extremal problem, find the maximum possible area of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle of radius \( R = 5 \).
en.hint: By Jensen's inequality on \( \frac{{1}}{{2}}R^2 \sum \sin\theta_i \), the area is maximized when the quadrilateral is regular (a square of area \( 2R^2 \)).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Among all n-gons inscribed in a circle of radius R, the regular n-gon maximizes area; for n = 4, Area_max = 2 R^2.

Step 1: Substitute \( R = 5 \): \( \text{Area}_{\max} = 2 \times 5^2 = 50 \).

✅ Quick Check: Maximal inscribed quadrilateral area verified: \( 50 \).

ar.question: في مسألة القيم القصوى للمضلعات المحاطة بدائرة في الأولمبياد المتقدم، أوجد أكبر مساحة ممكنة لشكل رباعي محاط بدائرة نصف قطرها \( R = 5 \).
ar.hint: باستخدام متباينة ينسن على \( \frac{{1}}{{2}}R^2 \sum \sin\theta_i \)، تبلغ المساحة قيمتها العظمى عندما يكون الرباعي منتظماً (مربع مساحته \( 2R^2 \)).

💡 الفكرة الأساسية: بين جميع الرباعيات المحاطة بدائرة نصف قطرها R، يحقق المربع أكبر مساحة وتساوي 2 R^2.

en.hint: Since \( 4 \mid 12 \), the Turán graph \( T(12, 4) \) has \( \left(1 - \frac{1}{4}\right)\frac{12^2}{2} \) edges.
en.explanation:

Step 1: Evaluate \( \frac{4-1}{2 \cdot 4} \times 12^2 = 54 \).

✅ Quick Check: Turán edge count verified: \( 54 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Ramsey Theory problem, what is the exact two-color Ramsey number \( R(3, 3) \)?
en.hint: Use the recursive upper bound \( R(s, t) \le R(s-1, t) + R(s, t-1) \) (with strict inequality when both summands are even).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Two-color Ramsey numbers satisfy R(3,3)=6, R(3,4)=9, R(3,5)=14, R(4,4)=18, and R(2,t)=t.

Step 1: By classic extremal degree parity and Erdős-Szekeres recursion, \( R(3, 3) = 6 \).

✅ Quick Check: Exact Ramsey number verified: \( 6 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad double-counting incidence problem on a bipartite graph \( G = (U, V, E) \), \( |U| = 12 \), every vertex in \( U \) has degree \( 5 \), and \( |V| = 10 \). If every vertex in \( V \) has the same degree \( d \), find \( d \).
en.hint: Count incidences from both sides: \( |U| \cdot \deg(u) = |E| = |V| \cdot d \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: By double counting edges across the bipartite partition, sum_{u in U} deg(u) = sum_{v in V} deg(v).

Step 1: Thus \( 12 \times 5 = 10 d \), giving \( d = 6 \).

✅ Quick Check: Bipartite degree balance verified: \( 6 \).

ar.hint: احسب الوقوعات من كلا الطرفين: \( |U| \cdot \deg(u) = |E| = |V| \cdot d \).
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: بالعد المزدوج للأضلاع عبر جزأي البيان الثنائي يتساوى مجموعا الدرجات.

الخطوة 1: إذن \( 12 \times 5 = 10 d \)، ومنه \( d = 6 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تم التحقق من توازن الدرجات: \( 6 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad double-counting incidence problem on a bipartite graph \( G = (U, V, E) \), \( |U| = 15 \), every vertex in \( U \) has degree \( 4 \), and \( |V| = 12 \). If every vertex in \( V \) has the same degree \( d \), find \( d \).
en.hint: Count incidences from both sides: \( |U| \cdot \deg(u) = |E| = |V| \cdot d \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: By double counting edges across the bipartite partition, sum_{u in U} deg(u) = sum_{v in V} deg(v).

Step 1: Thus \( 15 \times 4 = 12 d \), giving \( d = 5 \).

✅ Quick Check: Bipartite degree balance verified: \( 5 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad extremal incidence design problem, \( n \) club members form \( n \) committees of \( 3 \) members each such that every pair of members serves together on at most one committee. Find the maximum possible \( n \) when every pair meets on exactly one committee.
en.hint: Double-count pairs of members inside committees: \( n \binom{3}{2} = \binom{n}{2} \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Counting point-pairs per block gives n * C(k, 2) <= C(n, 2), with equality when n - 1 = k(k - 1).

Step 1: Solving \( n - 1 = 3(3 - 1) = 6 \) gives \( n = 7 \).

✅ Quick Check: Symmetric incidence configuration verified: \( 7 \).

en.hint: Double-count pairs of members inside committees: \( n \binom{4}{2} = \binom{n}{2} \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Counting point-pairs per block gives n * C(k, 2) <= C(n, 2), with equality when n - 1 = k(k - 1).

Step 1: Solving \( n - 1 = 4(4 - 1) = 12 \) gives \( n = 13 \).

✅ Quick Check: Symmetric incidence configuration verified: \( 13 \).

ar.question: في مسألة تصميم الوقوع القصوي للأولمبياد المتقدم، يشكّل \( n \) عضواً \( n \) لجنة تضم كل منها \( 6 \) أعضاء بحيث يشترك كل زوج من الأعضاء في لجنة واحدة على الأكثر. أوجد قيمة \( n \) عندما يشترك كل زوج في لجنة واحدة بالضبط.
ar.hint: استخدم العد المزدوج لأزواج الأعضاء داخل اللجان: \( n \binom{6}{2} = \binom{n}{2} \).
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: عدّ الأزواج داخل اللجان يعطي n * C(k, 2) = C(n, 2)، أي n = k(k - 1) + 1.

الخطوة 1: بحل المعادلة \( n - 1 = 6(6 - 1) \) نحصل على \( n = 31 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تم التحقق من قيمة التصميم التوافقي: \( 31 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad extremal incidence design problem, \( n \) club members form \( n \) committees of \( 8 \) members each such that every pair of members serves together on at most one committee. Find the maximum possible \( n \) when every pair meets on exactly one committee.
en.hint: Double-count pairs of members inside committees: \( n \binom{8}{2} = \binom{n}{2} \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Counting point-pairs per block gives n * C(k, 2) <= C(n, 2), with equality when n - 1 = k(k - 1).

Step 1: Solving \( n - 1 = 8(8 - 1) = 56 \) gives \( n = 57 \).

✅ Quick Check: Symmetric incidence configuration verified: \( 57 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Sperner's Theorem problem, what is the maximum size of an antichain of subsets of \( \{1, 2, \dots, 6\} \) (where no subset contains another)?
en.hint: By Sperner's Theorem, the largest antichain has size \( \binom{6}{\lfloor 6/2 \rfloor} \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Extremal set theory bounds antichains via Sperner's theorem and intersecting k-families via Erdos-Ko-Rado.

Step 1: Evaluate the middle binomial coefficient \( \binom{6}{3} = 20 \).

✅ Quick Check: Extremal family size verified: \( 20 \).

ar.hint: حسب مبرهنة سبيرنر، أكبر عائلة غير متداخلة حجمها \( \binom{6}{\lfloor 6/2 \rfloor} \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تم التحقق من الحجم الأقصى للعائلة: \( 20 \).

💡 Key Idea: Extremal set theory bounds antichains via Sperner's theorem and intersecting k-families via Erdos-Ko-Rado.

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Erdős-Ko-Rado Theorem problem, find the maximum number of \( 3 \)-element subsets of \( \{1, 2, \dots, 7\} \) that are pairwise intersecting.
en.hint: For \( n \ge 2k \), the Erdős-Ko-Rado bound is \( \binom{n-1}{k-1} \).

💡 Key Idea: Extremal set theory bounds antichains via Sperner's theorem and intersecting k-families via Erdos-Ko-Rado.

Step 1: Compute \( \binom{7-1}{3-1} = \binom{6}{2} = 15 \).

✅ Quick Check: Extremal family size verified: \( 15 \).

en.hint: For \( n \ge 2k \), the Erdős-Ko-Rado bound is \( \binom{n-1}{k-1} \).

💡 Key Idea: Extremal set theory bounds antichains via Sperner's theorem and intersecting k-families via Erdos-Ko-Rado.

Step 1: Compute \( \binom{8-1}{3-1} = \binom{7}{2} = 21 \).

✅ Quick Check: Extremal family size verified: \( 21 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Burnside's Lemma problem, how many distinct necklaces of \( p = 3 \) beads can be formed using \( k = 2 \) colors up to cyclic rotation?
en.hint: For prime \( p \), Burnside's Lemma gives \( \frac{{1}}{{p}}\left(k^p + (p-1)k\right) \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Under C_p, the identity fixes k^p colorings and each of the p-1 non-trivial rotations fixes k monochromatic colorings.

Step 1: Compute \( (2^{3} + 2 \times 2) / 3 = 4 \).

✅ Quick Check: Burnside orbit count verified: \( 4 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad dihedral Pólya-Burnside problem, how many inequivalent ways can the \( 4 \) vertices of a square be colored with up to \( k = 2 \) colors under the full dihedral group \( D_4 \) of \( 8 \) rotations and reflections?
en.hint: Average fixed colorings over all \( 8 \) elements of \( D_4 \): \( \frac{{1}}{{8}}(k^4 + 2k^3 + 3k^2 + 2k) \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: In D_4 on 4 vertices: identity fixes k^4, two 90-deg rotations fix k, one 180-deg rotation fixes k^2, two side-bisector flips fix k^2, and two diagonal flips fix k^3.

en.hint: Average fixed colorings over all \( 8 \) elements of \( D_4 \): \( \frac{{1}}{{8}}(k^4 + 2k^3 + 3k^2 + 2k) \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: In D_4 on 4 vertices: identity fixes k^4, two 90-deg rotations fix k, one 180-deg rotation fixes k^2, two side-bisector flips fix k^2, and two diagonal flips fix k^3.

Step 1: At \( k = 6 \), \( (6^4 + 2\cdot6^3 + 3\cdot6^2 + 2\cdot6)/8 = 231 \).

✅ Quick Check: Dihedral orbit count verified: \( 231 \).

الخطوة 1: عند \( k = 6 \) نجد أن الناتج هو \( 231 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تم التحقق من عدد التلوينات تحت D_4: \( 231 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad generating function problem, find the coefficient \( [x^{8}] \frac{1}{(1 - x)^{4}} \) in the formal power series expansion.
en.hint: By the negative binomial series identity, \( [x^n](1-x)^{-k} = \binom{n+k-1}{k-1} \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: The generating function 1/(1 - x)^k counts multisets of size n from k types, so [x^n] 1/(1 - x)^k = C(n + k - 1, k - 1).

Step 1: Compute \( \binom{8+4-1}{4-1} = \binom{11}{3} = 165 \).

✅ Quick Check: Generating function coefficient verified: \( 165 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Linearity of Expectation problem, a random permutation \( \pi \) of \( \{1, 2, \dots, 8\} \) awards \( 8 \) points for each fixed point \( \pi(i) = i \). Find the expected total score.
en.hint: By linearity of expectation, the expected number of fixed points in a uniform random permutation of \( n \) elements is always \( 1 \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Each element i is fixed with probability 1/n, so E[fixed points] = n * (1/n) = 1.

Step 1: Multiplying the expected \( 1 \) fixed point by \( 8 \) points per fixed point gives \( 8 \).

✅ Quick Check: Linearity of expectation verified: \( 8 \).

ar.question: في مسألة خطية التوقع الرياضي للأولمبياد المتقدم، يمنح تبديل عشوائي \( \pi \) للمجموعة \( \{1, 2, \dots, 8\} \) عدد \( 8 \) نقطة عن كل نقطة ثابتة تحقق \( \pi(i) = i \). أوجد القيمة المتوقعة لمجموع النقاط.
ar.hint: بفضل خطية التوقع، العدد المتوقع للنقاط الثابتة في تبديل عشوائي منتظم لـ \( n \) عنصراً يساوي دائماً \( 1 \).
ar.explanation:

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad random permutation problem, what is the expected number of maximal ascending contiguous runs in a uniformly random permutation of \( \{1, 2, \dots, 13\} \)?
en.hint: A new ascending run begins at index \( 1 \) and at each descent \( \pi(i) > \pi(i+1) \), which occurs with probability \( 1/2 \) at each of the \( 13-1 \) adjacent pairs.
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: By indicator variables on the n - 1 adjacent pairs, E[runs] = 1 + (n - 1)/2 = (n + 1)/2.

Step 1: Compute \( 1 + (13 - 1)/2 = (13 + 1)/2 = 7 \).

✅ Quick Check: Expected run count verified: \( 7 \).

en.question: In a Senior Olympiad Probabilistic Method (Caro-Wei theorem) problem, a \( 2 \)-regular graph \( G \) has \( n = 12 \) vertices. What lower bound on the independence number \( \alpha(G) \) is guaranteed by \( \sum_{{v \in V}} \frac{{1}}{{\deg(v) + 1}} \)?
en.hint: In a uniformly random vertex ordering, vertex \( v \) precedes all \( \deg(v) \) of its neighbors with probability \( 1/(\deg(v)+1) \).
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: By the Caro-Wei probabilistic proof, alpha(G) >= sum_{v in V} 1/(deg(v) + 1).

✅ Quick Check: Caro-Wei lower bound verified: \( 4 \).

en.hint: In a uniformly random vertex ordering, vertex \( v \) precedes all \( \deg(v) \) of its neighbors with probability \( 1/(\deg(v)+1) \).

💡 Key Idea: By the Caro-Wei probabilistic proof, alpha(G) >= sum_{v in V} 1/(deg(v) + 1).

✅ Quick Check: Caro-Wei lower bound verified: \( 5 \).
